description.summary: protocol for monitoring user idle time

protocol.description:
This protocol allows clients to monitor when the user is idle, that is, has not used keyboard, mouse or touch for a while, so that they can blank the screen, lock the session or put the computer to sleep.
The protocol is used by hde-idle (src/hde-idle.c), the part of HDE that does that on the "HDE (Wayland)" session; on the "HDE" (X11) session the same daemon asks the XScreenSaver extension instead.
This is the ext-idle-notify-v1 protocol as published by the wayland-protocols project; the file is kept here, next to ext-session-lock-v1.xml, so that wayland-scanner can generate the client header without wayland-protocols being installed at build time.

interface.name: ext_idle_notifier_v1

description.summary: allows to monitor when the user is idle

interface.description: This interface allows the client to monitor the user's idle state.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request destroys the notifier. All notifications created by it become inert.

request.name: get_idle_notification

description.summary: create a new idle notification object

request.description: The notification object has a minimum timeout and fires ext_idle_notification_v1.idled when the seat has been idle for that many milliseconds, and ext_idle_notification_v1.resumed as soon as the user uses the seat again.

interface.name: ext_idle_notification_v1
interface.description: This interface is a handle to a single idle timeout.

event.name: idled
event.description: The notification is active: the seat has not been used for the timeout given when this object was created.

event.name: resumed

description.summary: the user is no longer idle

event.description: The notification is no longer active: the seat has been used again.
